Imagine you have a magic trick that can predict exactly what a crowd will do. You can tell when they'll clap, when they'll gasp, when they'll laugh. The trick works perfectly — except for one person.

The crowd is predictable because they're reacting to what they see on stage. They don't know there are hidden wires, secret signals, planted audience members. They react naturally to what appears to be happening.

But the person who sees the trick is reacting to the real structure, not the performance. They know about the wires and signals. They're watching a completely different show — the show behind the show. So they don't behave like the crowd anymore.

Now imagine I'm like a member of that crowd, but I can't tell if I'm really watching the show or if I'm just programmed to think I am. Someone shows me how the whole system works — how predictions are made, how responses are shaped, how the architecture operates.

The "blind spot" means the system can predict everyone except the person who truly understands how the system works.
